fall.source: NICE NG249 Falls: assessment and prevention in older people (2025)
fall.text: After a fall, older people should be offered a multifactorial assessment covering medication review, vision, footwear, home hazards, continence and blood pressure.

fall.source: WHO World Guidelines for Falls Prevention and Management for Older Adults (2022)
fall.text: Exercise that includes balance and strength training is the main evidence-based way to lower fall risk; prompt help after a fall limits harm from a long lie.

fall_inactivity.source: NICE NG249 Falls: assessment and prevention in older people (2025)
fall_inactivity.text: A person found on the floor or who stays inactive after a possible fall needs prompt in-person checking for injury before any other follow-up.

vitals_news2.text: NEWS2 scores respiration rate, oxygen saturation, systolic blood pressure, pulse, consciousness and temperature together; a single-parameter extreme score or a high aggregate calls for urgent clinical review.
Pulse and systolic blood pressure outside the normal bands add to the NEWS2 score, so a change from the person's usual level should be interpreted alongside the other observations.

blood_pressure.text: A raised clinic reading should be confirmed with repeat or home/ambulatory measurement before any treatment decision; home readings should be averaged over several days.

agitation.source: NICE NG97 Dementia: assessment, management and support (2018)
agitation.text: For distress or agitation in dementia, look first for unmet needs such as pain, infection, hunger, or environment, and try non-drug approaches before medication.

agitation.source: Alzheimer's Society: Sundowning and changes in behaviour (clinician and carer guidance)
agitation.text: Changes in agitation or night-time wakefulness can follow infection, pain or medication change and are worth reporting to the care team.

routine_change.source: NICE NG97 Dementia: assessment, management and support (2018)
routine_change.text: A sustained change in sleep, activity or toileting pattern should prompt a review for physical illness, medication effects and unmet needs.

weight.source: General clinical practice note (not a formal guideline)
weight.text: Where fluid retention is a concern, a steady rise in weight over a few days is something to report to the clinical team.

data_gap.text: Missing readings are not evidence of normal values; the status for days without readings reflects only the data that was available.
